summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour presents a detailed hadith narration describing the appearance and characteristics of the believers who will enter paradise. He explains that the first group will have the appearance of a full moon on the clearest night, while the second group will resemble the brightest star in the sky. Sh. Ali Mashhour uses this as an opportunity to reflect on modern light pollution and humanity's attempt to control nature through technology like electricity and light bulbs. He then elaborates on the physical characteristics of paradise, including descriptions of the inhabitants' perfect bodies, their garments and vessels made of gold, the fragrance of their sweat being musk, and the presence of maidens. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that paradise will be customized to each person's desires, and that the descriptions given are analogies representing the ultimate beauty and perfection of paradise that transcends cultural standards of beauty.
suggested_title: The Descriptions of Paradise: Physical Perfection and Divine Customization
catchy_title: What Will Paradise Really Look Like?
